tex_content.html:
Corollary
↗ thm:synge-positive-sectional 1. ch12:12.33

Let $(M,g)$ be compact, connected, even-dimensional, and strictly positively curved. If $M$ is orientable then $\pi _1(M)=0$; otherwise $\pi _1(M)\cong \mathbb Z/2$.

Proof

\sketch The orientable case is Synge’s theorem. In the nonorientable case, the two-sheeted orientable cover is simply connected by Synge, hence universal; its fibers have two points, so the fundamental group is $\mathbb Z/2$.

□
